title: Tenant-aware export priority lanes and delivery patterns for high-volume reporting requests
creator: Aisha Rao
body:
Background:
Enterprise customers are increasingly requesting scheduled and ad-hoc exports of token-level usage, per-route cost breakdowns, and tenant-scoped time-series for chargeback and compliance. Current intake routes are ad-hoc (email/slack) and small-tenant oriented; we lack a clear priority routing model, delivery SLA tiers, and a standardized data contract for exports. This results in engineering ad-hoc work, missed expectations, and manual reconciliation for billing teams.

Objective:
Define a tenant-aware intake and prioritization playbook that:
- Classifies export requests into priority lanes (Self-serve, Scheduled, Enterprise SLA, Critical Compliance)
- Specifies delivery patterns (immediate API export, daily S3 drop, scheduled BigQuery/Redshift push) and estimated SLAs per lane
- Produces a minimal, enforceable data contract for usage and cost exports (fields, granularity, timezone rules, retention)
- Establishes routing ownership (PM triage -> Solutions Eng -> Platform/Eng) and developer acceptance criteria for engineering work

Scope (in-scope):
- Request types: per-workspace token usage, per-route cost breakdown, aggregated tenant usage by month/day/hour, and CSV/Parquet/S3/BQ delivery targets.
- Priority lanes and associated SLA/expected turnarounds.
- Data contract draft and validation checklist for exports.
- Telemetry/observability requirements for export jobs (success/failure rates, latency bins, data volume metrics).

Out of scope (for this ticket):
- Full implementation of backend push connectors (BQs/Redshift pipelines) — will be captured as follow-up ENG tickets.
- Deep cost-modeling for each tenant — billing team will own pricing decisions.

Success metrics:
- 90% of enterprise export requests are assigned to a lane within 48 hours of intake.
- 80% of requests routed to "Enterprise SLA" lane have documented data contract signoff within 2 weeks.
- Reduce ad-hoc engineering task time spent on exports by 50% (measured via ENG time entries / PR count).

Priority lanes (proposal):
1) Self-serve (low friction): Customer can generate CSV/Parquet exports in Console for last 7/30/90 days. Target SLA: instant to 1 hour.
2) Scheduled (medium): Customers request daily/weekly exports to S3 with a standard schema. Target SLA: 5 business days to enable.
3) Enterprise SLA (high): Tenant requires recurring exports with SLAs, encryption/KMS, schema guarantees, and customer-managed delivery endpoints. Target SLA: 10 business days initial enablement + formal data contract signoff.
4) Compliance/Critical (urgent): Legal/audit requests requiring retention-limited extracts or forensics. Target SLA: 48 hours with priority ops involvement.

Data contract (minimum fields):
- workspace_id, workspace_name, tenant_id, timestamp_utc, request_id, model_name, route, tokens_input, tokens_output, token_cost_micro_usd, billed_amount_usd, project_tag (optional), zone (region), export_version.
- Granularity: event-level with optional daily aggregation.
- Timezone handling: all timestamps in UTC; provide local timezone mapping column when requested.
- Schema versioning: exports must expose "export_version" and support backward-compatible changes.

Intake flow (operational):
- Customer files request via Console "Reporting Requests" form (fields: desired lane, delivery pattern, example data sink, retention, security controls).
- PM triage reviews within 48 hours, assigns lane and owner (Solutions Eng for enterprise).
- For Enterprise SLA and Compliance lanes, require data contract signoff and security checklist (KMS, IP allowlist) before scheduling engineering work.

Engineering acceptance criteria (hand-off checklist):
- Data contract signed and attached to the ticket.
- Delivery pattern and destination credentials verified (or placeholder for dev-testing).
- Success/failure metrics defined and dashboard created in Console.
- Test vectors and sample export validated by QA.

Telemetry & Observability requirements:
- Export job status events (submitted, started, succeeded, failed) with job_id.
- Per-job latency histogram, row counts, bytes written.
- Alerting: failure rate >5% over 24h or median latency > SLA threshold -> paging to on-call.

Security & Compliance considerations:
- Enterprise exports to customer-owned sinks must enforce server-side encryption and optional KMS key usage.
- Audit logs for export requests and who approved data contracts.
- Handle PII-sensitive exports via redaction or SOC/Legal-approved pathways only.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Draft playbook, data contract template, Console intake form mock.
- Week 2: Review with Solutions Eng and Billing; iterate.
- Week 3: Pilot with 2 existing enterprise customers (one needing scheduled S3, one needing BigQuery push).
- Week 4-6: Collect feedback, refine schema and telemetry, create ENG tickets for connector work.

Open questions / risks:
- How many export schema versions do we need to support simultaneously?
- Need to quantify engineering effort for different delivery patterns (S3 vs BQ/Redshift).
- Pricing/packaging implications for scheduled/enterprise lanes — coordinate with RevOps.

Next steps:
- Align with Solutions Eng and Billing on proposed lanes (owner: Liam O'Connell).
- Build Console intake mock and copy (owner: Aisha Rao).
- Raise ENG scoping ticket for initial S3 scheduled export connector (suggest ENG-4218).
